primitives.name: Rowing Velocity Profile
primitives.verbatim_quote: ROWING 69 point at which the crew can row, this varying with different styles of rowing: the present average is about 34 to 36, except on spurts.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v': 'm/s, average rowing speed', 't': 's, time interval', 'S': 'stroke rate (strokes per second)'}

primitives.name: Fault Placement in Pair-Oar
primitives.verbatim_quote: If, as is almost invariably the case, some man finds himself the possessor of an obstinate fault, the place for him is the pair-oar, no matter at what season of the year.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f': 'dimensionless fault severity index', 'p': 'position in crew (1 to 8)', 'o': 'pair-oar configuration indicator'}
primitives.assumptions: Faults are localized and correctable in pair-oar setup; crew dynamics decouple during training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When f > 0.7, optimal placement is pair-oar regardless of season.

layer2.mapping: GSI models fault propagation through crew configurations; GSE assigns corrective actions based on position.
layer2.telemetry: Fault detection logs and crew positioning data

primitives.name: Training Efficiency Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: Either with his coach or alone, he can often find and remedy the difficulty in a short time, whereas in the cranky and rapidly moving shell he is completely at a loss how to act.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E': 'dimensionless training efficiency', 'T': 'time spent correcting fault (s)', 'R': 'rate of correction (s⁻¹)'}
primitives.assumptions: Training efficiency increases inversely with dynamic instability of shell.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R < 0.5 s⁻¹, training becomes ineffective due to motion-induced error.

layer2.mapping: GSI computes E(T) for adaptive coaching algorithms; GSE evaluates E(T) for real-time feedback loops.
layer2.telemetry: Correction time and motion stability metrics
